<reason>A more convincingly challenged the proposition’s combined promise. Its compliant-employer/evasive-contractor comparison explained how limited employment reductions and substantial recruitment problems could coexist, defeating B’s claimed contradiction. Seasonal whole-crew hiring also directly weakened B’s gradual-adjustment defense. B offered plausible deterrence mechanisms and legitimately pressed for evidence of large harms, but overread state departures as national employment reductions and repeatedly mischaracterized conditional arguments as concessions. Its accusation of unanswered questions was also premature in the actual chronology. A’s limited direct evidence of harm keeps this a competitive win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A distinguished pre-offer discrimination from abuse recorded after hiring. B subsequently acknowledged that verification logs address post-hire conduct and invoked separate enforcement tools, undermining its original claim that E-Verify’s audit trail itself makes rejected applicants’ exclusion detectable.</best_rebuttal>
